# NOTES ON "HOPE LESLIE; OR, EARLY TIMES IN THE MASSACHUSETTS" (Catharine Maria Sedgwick, 1842, 2 vols, Harper & Brothers)

Source metadata: Gutenberg 76028 and 76018, public domain. Epigraph (both vols): Indian chieftain verse ending "Where has the rainbow vanished?--there does the Indian dwell.--E."

## VOLUME I

**Ch I (England, then Springfield/Boston).** Sir William Fletcher, eminent lawyer, wants nephew William Fletcher to marry daughter Alice; writes brother warning against Puritans, Liberty ("Daughter of Disloyalty"), neighbours Winthrop and Eliot. William is friend of Winthrop (Groton) and Eliot. Sir William makes engagement conditional on William abjuring liberty/religion and swearing loyalty to king and Established Church. William flees, sails from Southampton. Alice follows him aboard; Sir William's guards seize her from the strand; William returns to London, interview with uncle. Alice is forced to marry Charles Leslie. William marries Winthrop's orphan ward (Martha, later Mrs. Fletcher) and emigrates in 1630 in ship Arbella with Winthrop. Alice later emigrates with two daughters, dies at sea; her will commits children (Hope and Faith Leslie) to William's guardianship. Sister of Leslie: Mrs. Grafton (Dame Bertha Grafton, Dame Grafton).

**Ch II (Springfield, 1636 onward).** Fletcher settles at "Bethel," a mile from Springfield (Pynchon, Holioke, Chapin founders). Son Everell (14). Wife Martha. Letter from Governor Winthrop brings news; Alice dead; the Leslie girls coming. Indian girl Magawisca (15), daughter of Pequod chief Mononotto, sister of Oneco (boy servant), with mother Monoca/Monoco, given as spoil to English; Magawisca speaks English taught by English captive. Servant Digby (Fletcher's domestic) and Jennet (serving-woman, sour, pious). Digby brings Pequod chief Sassacus's scalp (not Mononotto's) from Pynchon; Magawisca distressed; Indian messenger carries her bracelet to father, says Mononotto lives among the Mohawks.

**Ch III.** Fletcher goes to Boston, returns after nine days. Companions: Mrs. Grafton (widow, Anglican, vain of fashion, "peculiar" is her word) and Master Cradock (tutor, "skilled in the tongues"). Wards renamed Hope (Hope Leslie, eldest, bright) and Faith (youngest, Mary, shy, petted). Baptized by Mr. Cotton. Martha's letter to Fletcher (1638) reports: Mrs. Grafton; prank with prayer-book during wolves storm (Everell); Magawisca's aversion; Oneco brings game; servant Hutton punished (twenty stripes; "Toper" board); Darby; Indians lurking; Nelema (old Indian woman) visits Martha with baby, prophesies; Magawisca drops snake rattle, arrow (symbols of danger). Everell and Magawisca on night watch with Digby.

**Ch IV.** Night watch at Bethel. Magawisca goes to Nelema's hut; returns; eagle feather. Digby and Everell hear footsteps. Magawisca tells of Pequod massacre (her mother Monoco, brother Samoset killed, Cushmakin, Wequash the traitor, Narragansetts, Sassacus, father Mononotto's revenge). Digby: "hawks won't pick out hawks' eyes." Mononotto's motives explained.

**Ch V.** Fletcher expected home; Hutton's and Digby's errands; Mrs. Grafton's pony ride to Holioke with bandbox; Digby sent away. Mrs. Fletcher and children on portico; Hope's arrival expected. Mononotto and three warriors attack; Magawisca and Oneco cry "My father!"; Magawisca shields Mrs. Fletcher; Mrs. Fletcher killed with baby (infant boy dashed on door-stone); Everell fights, rings horn alarm. Faith Leslie, Oneco, Everell, and Magawisca taken; Oneco's English dress removed.

**Ch VI.** Hutton and Digby return; Jennet hiding in bedroom chimney. Digby bloodied trail. Pynchon pursues. Fletcher arrives, Hope carried on litter by Indians; Pynchon tells Fletcher; Fletcher goes alone to Bethel; Hope left with Pynchon. Bodies. Puritan funeral. Mononotto's flight; Everell kept captive. Magawisca's pleas refused ("cries are for children and cowards"). Night escape attempt; Digby and six men in canoe (Lawrence, John Wilkin); Digby says must find "the boy."

**Ch VII.** Journey through Berkshire hills; Housatonic valley; village with chief; Magawisca's prophecy; Mononotto's sacrifice-rock ritual at sunrise; Everell ready to die; Magawisca's sleeping potion for Mohawk guard; she climbs rock, severs arm? (Her arm is cut off by the blow aimed at Everell), Everell escapes.

**Ch VIII.** Letter from Hope to Everell in England (seven years later). Hope paints Everell's sleeping-with-wolf picture; Digby jovial; Mrs. Grafton's silver; Winthrop; Mr. Holioke names "Mount Holioke"; Cradock bitten by rattlesnake on Mount Holioke; Hope proposes sucking poison; Nelema cures him with snake-symbol rite; Jennet's accusation; Winthrop and Mr. Fletcher question Hope about witchcraft. Nelema sentenced by Pynchon, Holioke, Chapin; Hope escapes Nelema from Pynchon's cellar; Digby ferries her. Hope sent to Boston to Madam Winthrop. Mrs. Grafton's letter to Everell (pills, "feuille morte," "Lady Penyvere"). Hope's dream of Nelema: "I will reach there."

**Ch IX.** Explanation of Nelema's release. Hope described (height, hair, eyes). Everell returns to Boston on pilot-boat with Sir Philip Gardiner (self-styled Puritan knight, with page Roslin). They see Hope; she greets Everell; Miss Esther Downing (daughter of Emanuel Downing, Winthrop's brother-in-law) walks with her. Boston geography.

**Ch X.** Hope and Esther talk. Esther's back-story: she loved Everell in Suffolk-era visit; he left after her illness, she confessed to him; he believed her death-bed. Esther's maid Judy. Jennet grumbles. Dinner: Everell says "Esther" compliment; Winthrop rebukes.

**Ch XI.** Governor Winthrop's house described; Madam Winthrop; Indians Miantunnomoh (Narragansett) at dinner; Cradock spills gravy. Sir Philip's compliment. Winthrop reads letter from Mr. Downing proposing Everell marry Esther; Mr. Fletcher agrees; Hubbard proposed for Hope; Sir Philip proposed by Winthrop.

**Ch XII.** Sabbath customs. Everell and Hope at lecture; Gorton prisoners; Mr. Cotton's sumptuary rule. Hope meets page Roslin in street ("the lost may warn"). Hope goes to the burying-ground for secret meeting; at mother's grave she prays; sees Magawisca.

**Ch XIII.** Storm; Hope returns soaked in Sir Philip's cloak; Everell sees her; Esther tearful; Hope says she won't reveal. Hope sends Esther away; Sir Philip's hint.

## VOLUME II

**Ch I.** Magawisca disguised as moccasin-seller meets Hope in hall; Jennet, Mrs. Grafton buy moccasins; Magawisca reveals identity; meeting set for Friday (five suns); Hope's promise. Sir Philip overhears from thicket.

**Ch II.** Sir Philip's letter to Wilton: former patron Thomas Morton (Merry Mount); Rosa (his disguised page, natural child of nobleman, Lady Lunford's ward); Sir Philip's scheme to seduce Hope. Rosa's breakdown; he soothes her.

**Ch III.** Week of anxiety. Friday garden excursion; Madam Winthrop's premonition; Everell escorts Esther. Hope gives Esther credit; Esther and Everell's rosebud gift; Hope tells Digby of "Everell's wedding"; Esther believes engagement; Hope rejects Sir Philip's advances in garden (Latin/French verses). Mrs. Grafton, Sir Philip. Everell tells Hope he's lost; Hope says "Esther."

**Ch IV.** Hope arranges with Digby; sees Magawisca's canoe; meets Mary (Faith) and Oneco; Magawisca interprets; rings offered; Mary refuses; Beacon Hill light; Sir Philip and boat party seize Magawisca and Mary; Oneco escapes with Hope. Storm; Sir Philip and Digby can't pursue. Everell and Esther in window; Winthrop: Magawisca arrested.

**Ch V.** Oneco's canoe in storm; Mononotto struck by lightning; Hope escapes to island; drunken sailors of Chaddock's crew; Hope escapes in boat; Antonio Batista, Italian sailor, thinks her a saint (Santa Petronilla); Roslin finds Hope faint; Everell and Fletcher find her.

**Ch VI.** Sir Philip's plot; Morton's cell; Magawisca's prison; Sir Philip offers rope ladder for her escape conditional on Rosa; Magawisca refuses; Morton attacks Sir Philip; Everell tries to free Magawisca but guard warns. Barnaby Tuttle the jailer. Sir Philip's backstory of Rosa.

**Ch VII.** Trial of Magawisca set; Hope recovers; Faith refuses finery; Hope's confession to Winthrop; Hope pleads for Magawisca; Esther confronts Hope in tears; Everell asks Esther to help free Magawisca; Esther refuses on Scripture.

**Ch VIII.** Trial: Eliot prays; Sir Philip false testimony (Magawisca had crucifix); Rosa in court; Magawisca's appeal "In the name of God, liberty!"; trial adjourned.

**Ch IX.** Sir Philip's plan to frame Rosa; Jennet overhears Hope and Everell's plot, tells Sir Philip; Sir Philip plots to have Chaddock kidnap Hope.

**Ch X.** Evening; stranger (Oneco disguised) enters; Hope and Cradock go to jail; Hope swaps Magawisca with Cradock; Barnaby deceived; Magawisca escapes. Everell joins; Hope's "wig and boots" trick.

**Ch XI.** Chaddock's crew kidnap Jennet (mistaken for Hope). Sir Philip sails with Rosa and Chaddock; Rosa throws lamp into gunpowder; vessel explodes, all die.

**Ch XII.** Oneco takes Mononotto to Sachem's Head, then Moscutusett; Oneco's disguise; Jennet seized by Oneco at Winthrop's kitchen; Oneco's wife Faith escapes.

**Ch XIII.** Magawisca departs with Digby in canoe to Moscutusett; Hope gives her gold chain and Everell's miniature; Everell and Hope part.

**Ch XIV.** Family rejoices. Antonio's report. Rosa and Sir Philip letters. Jennet's body found. Pardons: Hope, Cradock pardoned; Everell public censure. Esther writes farewell letter; Esther releases Everell; Hope and Everell marry. Mrs. Grafton dies in England. Digby, Barnaby provided for. Esther later unmarried.

## NOTES (end of each volume)
Vol I notes: (1) Pequod maiden interpreter; (2) Monoca virtues (Trumbull); (3) sachems beheaded; (4) Heckewelder quote; (5) Miantunnomoh's table (Winthrop); (6) Johnson's burial, Lady Arbella. Vol II notes: (7) Eliot, apostle of New-England; (8) Magawisca's reply; (9) Moscutusett etymology. Endnotes: [1] mice gnawed Prayer-book (Winthrop journal), [2] wekolis = whippoorwill, [3] Bryant verse on high places, [4] "help" plural.
